Arrive in Buenos Aires. Your driver meets you at the airport and takes you to your hotel.

Argentina’s capital stretches along the Río de la Plata and served as the country’s main gateway for centuries. Its neighborhoods each have their own architecture and atmosphere. San Telmo still has its old houses and cafés. Palermo is known for its restaurants, and Recoleta for its elegant streets and famous cemetery.

On the first day, you can take a stroll, watch the city go by, stop for coffee or spend the evening resting after your flight. Buenos Aires is a gentle start before the more active part of the trip. In two days, the route heads far south, where you’ll spend more time in nature and cover longer distances.
White obelisk amid wide roads and dense development in Buenos Aires, Argentina
Buenos Aires: an aerial view of the Obelisk and the city’s avenues

After breakfast, you’ll take a private sightseeing tour lasting about three hours with an English-speaking guide.

You’ll see La Boca and historic San Telmo, with its bars, restaurants and the antiques market at Plaza Dorrego. The route then takes you to Plaza de Mayo and Casa Rosada, the presidential palace associated with Evita Perón.

One of the city’s main landmarks is the 67-meter Obelisk on Avenida 9 de Julio. The tour includes Recoleta, with its famous cemetery, El Pilar Church and its cultural and commercial center. You’ll also see the modern districts of Puerto Madero, Lezama Park and Tres de Febrero Park.

Buenos Aires is known for its museums, galleries, theaters and architectural landmarks. Old port neighborhoods sit alongside broad avenues and a modern waterfront.

In the evening, enjoy a tango show with dinner. Tango emerged in the port districts among poor immigrants and gauchos. It was danced differently at first. Later came orchestras and a more elaborate stage style. Today it remains one of Argentina’s most recognizable cultural symbols. The restaurant serves traditional dishes and Argentine wines.
